value.body: An oilfield field engineer leads a small crew that delivers one specialised service at a well — such as wireline logging, cementing, well testing or stimulation. Oilfield service companies hire them to work for oil and gas operators. Days are long and irregular when a job is running, and are spent preparing equipment and reports at the base between jobs.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech in Petroleum, Mechanical, Electrical or ECE

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Long field rotations, onshore and offshore, sometimes abroad

items.label: India's domestic crude oil production
items.note: Down from ~34.2 million tonnes in 2018-19; ageing fields are one reason given
items.source: PRS Legislative Research, citing PPAC / MoPNG data

items.label: Share of crude oil requirement that India imports
items.note: Context for domestic exploration and production activity

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Service companies hire freshers as field engineer trainees, mostly through campus placement, followed by a structured training period. A valid passport and willingness to relocate and travel are usually expected.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Leading a small crew on site

value.title: At a glance
items: The lifestyle is demanding; many move to office roles after a few years.
Common next roles: senior field engineer, service quality or technical support, operations or sales.
Hiring is cyclical and tracks oil-and-gas activity.
